In [[cryptography]], '''Mercy''' is a tweakable [[block cipher]] designed by Paul Crowley for [[disk encryption]].

The [[block size (cryptography)|block size]] is 4096 bits—unusually large for a block cipher, but a standard [[disk sector]] size. Mercy uses a 128-bit secret [[key (cryptography)|key]], along with a 128-bit non-secret tweak for each block. In disk encryption, the sector number would be used as a tweak. Mercy uses a 6-round [[Feistel network]] structure with partial [[key whitening]]. The round function uses a key-dependent [[state machine]] which borrows some structure from the [[stream cipher]] [[WAKE (cipher)|WAKE]], with key-dependent [[S-box]]es based on the [[Kaisa Nyberg|Nyberg]] S-boxes also used in [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]].

[[Scott Fluhrer]] has discovered a [[differential attack]] that works against the full 6 rounds of Mercy.  This attack can even be extended to a seven-round variant.<ref name=fluhrer/>
